title: Book One · Chapter 33: Your Turn
story:
Jun hears about the flying kite on Friday. He doesn't ask Ronan at once. At break, he stands by the window desk and looks at the blue arrow.

"Did it really go up?"

"Really," Leo says. "Higher than the wall."

Jun points to the drawing. He keeps his hand away from the blue line. "Was it hard?"

"At first," Ronan says. "Then it was still a bit hard."

Jun smiles. He tells them his mother has work on Saturday morning, but she might take him to the drying yard in the afternoon.

Ronan almost says he will make Jun another kite by then. He wants to say yes at once. Then he remembers the work. He can offer Jun a turn instead. First he needs to ask Leo.

"You can try our kite. Leo, is that all right?"

Leo looks surprised. This time, Ronan asked him first. Then Leo nods. "With one of our mums there. We need a free space in the yard too."

Jun needs to wait for wind and a free yard. He will need an adult there, too. He nods and agrees. He goes to tell his mother at pickup time.

On Saturday, three children and two mothers meet at the yard. Dad has paid work for the morning. He can't come, and Ronan doesn't wait at the green gate hoping he will change that.

The wind is light. The kite stays on the board for a while. Jun holds the tail and looks disappointed.

"Is it broken again?"

"No wind yet," Leo says.

They play a quiet stone game on the clear ground. Each child tries to slide a smooth stone close to a chalk circle. Jun wins twice. His stone has one very flat side. Leo says that is unfair until Jun offers to swap stones for the next turn.

Then a breeze lifts the blue cloth.

Ronan and Leo set the line at the mark. The kite rises on the second try. Ronan holds it for a short time, then brings his hand low for Jun.

"Both hands first. Don't wrap it round your fingers."

Mum stands beside them. Ronan keeps a loose hand near the card until Jun feels the pull.

Jun's face changes. He looks up with a wide smile.

"It's strong."

"Not like a big dog," Leo says. "Don't fight it."

The kite dips. Jun pulls quickly. It dips farther.

Ronan wants to grab the card back. Instead, he puts his hand beside Jun's and helps him lower it a little. The paper stays still for a moment. Then the wind drops. The two boys bring the kite down together.

Jun is still smiling.

"I flew some of it."

"You did," Ronan says.

Jun's mother thanks the boys. She doesn't offer another coin. Nobody asks her for one.

On the way home, Leo says Jun held the line too tight.

"We held it too tight at first," Ronan says.

Leo thinks about that. Then he imitates his own first run, with shoulders high and feet going everywhere. Ronan laughs hard. He stops walking for a moment.

At the green gate, they check the paper for tears. There is a little dust on one corner. They brush it off and put the kite flat.

Jun flew their kite today. Now it is back at home. Ronan did not promise him another kite. There is no extra kite to finish tonight. He and Leo put their one kite away. Jun knows he can ask for another turn.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：turn＝轮到的一次；chalk＝粉笔；pull＝拉力；dust＝灰尘。

理解问题：

1. Ronan 怎样让 Jun 也参与试飞？
2. 这次分享和先前承诺做风筝有什么不同？
